area: Area 3: embedding similarity for the system's tasks
current_formulation: MMTEB evaluates embeddings on many tasks and languages and offers a zero-shot English benchmark without common training sets.

steps.formulation: STS shared tasks: annotators grade sentence pairs for semantic equivalence on a scale from 0 to 5.
steps.quote: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) assesses the degree to which two sentences are semantically equivalent to each other.

steps.formulation: STS Benchmark: one shared English training and evaluation set selected from the shared task data of 2012 to 2017.
steps.quote: the STS Benchmark is introduced as a new shared training and evaluation set

criticism.quote: STS is known to poorly correlate with other real-world use cases

steps.formulation: BEIR: zero-shot retrieval evaluation on datasets the models did not train on.
steps.quote: re-ranking and late-interaction based models on average achieve the best zeroshot performances

criticism.quote: Many BEIR datasets are found to be subject to a lexical bias

steps.formulation: MTEB: many task types in one benchmark, so that embeddings are tested beyond STS.
steps.quote: It is unclear whether state-of-the-art embeddings on semantic textual similarity (STS) can be equally well applied to other tasks like clustering or reranking.

criticism.quote: Text embeddings are typically evaluated on a limited set of tasks, which are constrained by language, domain, and task diversity.

steps.formulation: MMTEB: a multilingual benchmark with a zero-shot English version that excludes common training sets.
steps.quote: To prevent overfitting, we intend it as a zero-shot benchmark

criticism.quote: the benchmark may inadvertently encourage model developers to favor English or translated content
